cands.bio: Democratic candidate for Alabama House District 75 in 2026. She advanced from a canceled Democratic primary and lost the general election to incumbent Reed Ingram (R). Her occupation and any offices held are not documented in the sources reviewed.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as endorsed by two voter-guide groups: Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust (a Sway voting group run by Tabitha Isner) and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (a Sway voting group run by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Tisha Dickson Nickson was born or raised, or when she came to Alabama. We also couldn't find her occupation, education or any elected office she has held. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no other statement of her positions on data centers, property taxes, development, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing. We found no record of anything she has done in office, and no documented controversies or foreign ties.

cands.bio: Republican state representative for Alabama House District 75 (parts of Montgomery and Elmore counties) since November 2014. Car dealer by profession. Served on the Montgomery County Commission from 2004 to 2014. Former president of the Montgomery County Farm Bureau Federation.
cands.gaps: His birthplace, where he grew up, and when he came to Alabama are not stated in the pages we reviewed (only a birth year of 1962). We found no documented actions or stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B, campaign money pledges, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. The list of bills he sponsored did not load, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. We found no documented land-use stances, controversies, foreign ties, or notable endorsements for the 2026 race.
